text: The Patriots face a bruising Week 2 showdown with the Steelers, where Drake Maye will need to strike that delicate balance between patience and aggression against one of the league's most formidable defenses—a test that defines his developmental arc as a rookie. New England's secondary took a hit this week when Carlton Davis III was downgraded to out, forcing the Patriots to navigate Pittsburgh's pass rush without their starting cornerback, though the Steelers will be without starting wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), offering some measure of relief. On the bright side, running back TreVeyon Henderson, who missed the opener with an ankle injury, declared himself "ready to go" for Sunday, and the team elevated punter Mitch Wishnowsky from the practice squad for the second consecutive week to shore up special teams depth. The week also brought poignancy to the Patriots' organization as Stephon Gilmore, the franchise's two-time All-Pro and 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year, signed a one-day contract to retire as a New England Patriot, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest defensive backs in team history.
